newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY INCHES UP VS BASKET, BUT NO MAJOR TREND SEEN.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY INCHES UP VS BASKET, BUT NO MAJOR TREND SEEN.

text.p: The Polish zloty inched up against the basket in early trade but dealers said it lacked clear direction and the market was searching for a level where it would settle for the day.
They said the zloty was likely to stay within its last week's range of between one and 0.5 percent above the parity rate, changing along with dollar/mark moves.

"There is no real upward or downward pressure on the zloty. The market is probing various levels but the range of between one and 0.5 percent seems to hold," said Piotr Czyzewski of ING Bank in Warsaw.

At 0820 GMT the zloty was at 0.92/0.88 percent above the trading band centre, up from 0.80/0.69 percent at opening. It was at 3.2815/35 to the dollar and 1.8823/30 to the mark against 3.2900/40 and 1.8815/35 at opening respectively.
On the money market one-day bids eased some 0.1 point but offers held stable at 23.05/23.30 percent despite a net inflow of 100 million zlotys on Monday.
"The market seems to have priced in the increased likelihood of a rate rise of which the central bank was talking last week," one dealer said.
Dealers said that with rates above 23 percent the central bank was unlikely to stage any open market operations today.
Speculation on the rate rise potential is also likely to cut demand and make banks bid for higher yields at today's 1.2 billion zloty primary T-bill tender.
Dealers expect the 52-week maximum yield up 21.85-90 from 21.77 percent at the last tender, the 26-week bills up to 21.75-80 from 21.64 and 13-week paper up to 21.30-50 from 21.13 percent.
